newsitem.title: USA: Government drops charge against U.S. woman soldier.
newsitem.headline: Government drops charge against U.S. woman soldier.

text.p: The government on Sunday dropped false statement charges against a female private who recanted her rape charge against a sergeant involved in the Army's sex scandal at the Aberdeen Priving Ground.

At a summary court martial, Pvt. Toni Moreland pleaded guilty to charges with going Absent Without Leave (AWOL) and three lesser charges. She faces a maximum penalty of reduction to a lower pay grade, two months restriction, 45 days extra duty, forfeit of 20 days pay and confinement for 30 days.

Moreland was the first of five women who last month stepped forward to say she had been coerced into making false statements by Army investigators as a sexual abuse scandal unfolded on Army bases across the nation.
Acting Judge Capt. Christopher Eden said the charges against Moreland were not written properly and said that she was not told her rights before she gave a sworn statement.
Moreland's recanting of the statement triggered the congressional black caucus and the NAACP to ask for an independent investigation of the Army scandal.
Janice Grant, president of the Harford County NAACP, said the Army's decision to prosecute sergeants' sex offences was based on race.
"It seems to be that white people are sent away while black people are charged," she said. Moreland is white.
